comparator.name: Biologie (Biology)
comparator.sourceNotes: The current student curriculum fixes a three-year, 180-EC bachelor comprising a 135-EC Biology major and 45 EC of profiling space. The first year contains eight 7.5-EC courses: seven named compulsory foundations and one restricted first-year choice. After year one, only Academic Communication (level 2) and the 15-EC Afstudeerproject (level 3) remain compulsory; the remainder of the major is selected from Biology courses. The current study guide confirms that ordinary courses are 7.5 EC unless stated otherwise and that the Afstudeerproject is the 15-EC exception. The graduation-project page confirms that the compulsory project combines practical biological research, a report and presentation. The prospective curriculum presents eleven study-interest directions as advice for building a coherent programme, not formal tracks, so no direction is selected or named as the comparator route. The 52.5 EC of later Biology choice and 45 EC profiling space remain genuine choice space. These components account for exactly 180 EC without inventing electives.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad closest match covers the programme's full molecules-to-ecosystems identity. Two direct programme-interest clusters then support coherent, substantially distinct alternatives: molecular/cellular biology applied to health and computation, and ecology/evolution/conservation applied to environmental change. All three use feasible 24-course schedules and differ by well over four courses where required. Production stops at the maximum of three defensible alternatives.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both establish broad cellular and molecular foundations; UCR also integrates health and biomedical applications.
Both introduce evolution and biodiversity across major groups of life.
Both address animal structure and function; UCR concentrates on human physiology.
Both include microorganisms; UCR focuses on host–microbe interaction and immunity rather than plant biology.
Both combine ecological principles with modelling or experimental reasoning.
Both examine genes and genomes; UCR applies molecular genetics primarily to pathology.
The official first-year restricted choice remains open.
The programme's seven advanced Biology electives remain genuine choice space; the UCR routes instantiate different coherent biological emphases without claiming a formal UU track.
Both develop quantitative biological reasoning and statistics; UCR supplies a general mathematical-statistics sequence.
UCR develops scientific communication across courses rather than in one directly corresponding course.
The compulsory 15-EC Biology research project has no scheduled UCR course counterpart; UCR's optional independent research element is shown separately.
The genuine 45-EC profiling space is preserved without invented content.

notes.text: Utrecht Biology combines seven compulsory first-year foundations, flexible advanced Biology choices and a compulsory 15-EC research graduation project. UCR can assemble broad, molecular/biomedical and ecology/evolution programmes from current courses, but it does not reproduce Utrecht's dedicated organismal and plant sequence, its full specialist elective catalogue or its required graduation project; shared rows show substantive overlap rather than full equivalence.
